schema.name: Botulinum toxin treatment (Botox, Xeomin)
schema.howPerformed: Small units of botulinum toxin type A are injected into the specific muscles that fold the overlying skin, relaxing them for three to four months.

acceptedAnswer.text: The needle is very fine and each injection takes about a second. Most patients describe it as a brief sting. No anaesthetic is needed for a standard upper-face treatment.

mainEntity.name: How soon will I see it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Movement starts to soften at three to seven days and reaches its full effect at about fourteen days. Do not judge the result before two weeks.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Botox and Xeomin?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are botulinum toxin type A. Xeomin is formulated without the accessory proteins Botox carries, which is why it is often chosen for patients who appear to have stopped responding to Botox over time.

That is a dosing and placement decision, not a property of the drug. Dr. Stone treats the specific muscles that are folding the skin and leaves the rest working, and a first treatment is deliberately conservative.
